subject: Energy
title: Iron-Air Batteries
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Iron-Air Batteries.

hook.text: Iron-air batteries store energy by rusting iron—and release it by reversing the rust, using air as a reactant.

buildup.text: During discharge, iron pellets oxidize (rust)—during charge, electricity removes the oxygen, restoring pure iron.

discovery.text: Iron is the cheapest structural metal on Earth—making these batteries potentially 10x cheaper per kWh than lithium.

twist.text: Round-trip efficiency is about 45%—much lower than lithium-ion (90%), but acceptable for multi-day storage.

climax.text: Form Energy raised $800 million targeting 100-hour iron-air systems—designed to ride through multi-day weather events.

punchline.text: Rust and un-rust iron—the cheapest long-duration battery.

quiz.question: What chemical reaction powers an iron-air battery?
